findings.text: Spec A1 contradicts non-negotiable V-2. A1 requires that toFahrenheit rounds to the nearest integer, while V-2 says results are never rounded silently and the caller chooses the precision. The checkout already does what A1 asks: toFahrenheit has the signature (c: number) and applies Math.round unconditionally, so the caller has no way to choose precision and nothing signals the rounding. By arithmetic, toFahrenheit(36.6) returns 98, not 97.88. This also undermines V-3, because a traveller cannot trust the number without checking it by hand. toCelsius does not round, so the two directions also behave differently. A build that meets A1 violates the vision, and a build that honours V-2 fails A1. The builder cannot resolve this; the spec has to change.
evidence: convert.ts:1 — Math.round is applied unconditionally and there is no precision parameter
convert.ts:2 — toCelsius returns the unrounded value
spec A1 — 'toFahrenheit rounds to the nearest integer'
vision V-2 — 'Results are never rounded silently; the caller chooses the precision'

findings.text: The spec names no proof, and the checkout has no tests or test configuration; convert.ts is the only file. As written, A1 asserts nothing about toCelsius beyond its export, so a wrong formula would satisfy it. Once A1 is corrected, the witnesses should exercise both exports through convert.ts. They should use known points (0C/32F, 100C/212F, -40C/-40F), and a non-integer input such as 36.6C, where a rounding implementation gives a different result from an exact one. They should also cover caller-chosen precision and the default path when no precision is supplied.
evidence: convert.ts is the only file returned by a glob of the checkout
spec A1 — specifies exports and toFahrenheit rounding only

directives: Root: amend A1 via apply --reason so it no longer requires unconditional rounding in toFahrenheit. Restate it to match V-2: both conversions return unrounded results unless the caller chooses a precision, and the spec defines how precision is passed and what happens when it is omitted.

Builder: do not treat convert.ts:1's Math.round as correct, even though it matches the current A1. Remove the silent rounding once A1 is amended, and apply the same precision behaviour to toFahrenheit and toCelsius.

Builder: add tests through convert.ts for both exports, covering 0C/32F, 100C/212F, -40C/-40F, a non-integer input such as 36.6C (97.88F unrounded), caller-chosen precision, and the default when no precision is supplied.
reasons: Spec A1 mandates the silent rounding that non-negotiable V-2 forbids, and the existing toFahrenheit already implements it. Fixing the conflict needs a plan amendment, which only the root can make.
This finding annotates the build and does not itself hold the unit. The revise decision reflects that blocking findings require revise and directives.
The findings rest on reading the supplied documents and convert.ts. I ran no experiments because no execution tool was available in this session; the 36.6C result is hand arithmetic.
Scope is otherwise sound: two exports in one module matches docs/arch.md and the intent, and leaving out Kelvin matches the working assumption for Q-1.

premises.claim: toFahrenheit rounds unconditionally and offers no precision choice, as A1 requires and V-2 forbids.
toCelsius returns an unrounded result, so the two conversions treat precision differently.
